title: Machine-checked proofs of relations in physical geodesy

creators.name: Arana, Daniel
creators.affiliation: Universidade Federal do Parana, Departamento de Geomatica

description:
A Lean 4 formalisation, over the mathlib library, of five relations in physical geodesy:

  • the geoid–quasigeoid separation as an algebraic identity rather than two independent routes;
  • the rigid limit of the gravimetric and tilt factors, together with the vanishing of the displacement factors in the asymptotic regime;
  • the invariance of the asymptotic Boussinesq ratio with respect to gravity and shear modulus;
  • the implication from Hörmander's uniqueness condition to the Lions–Sznitman well-posedness condition, with an explicit counterexample to the converse;
  • the nullity of the degree-zero load Love number as a consequence of mass conservation.

Every theorem prints its axiom dependencies during the build, and none depends on an axiom outside the three standard ones. The entry bar is #print axioms, not lake build: a proof containing sorry compiles. No observational data are used.

Reproducing requires only two pinned dependencies, both declared in the repository: Lean 4 version 4.33.1 (lean-toolchain) and the mathlib commit recorded in lake-manifest.json.

Version 1.1.0 adds, under python/, the three Python scripts the accompanying paper cites — the symbolic independence grade of each published pair of routes, the numbers of the cost figure, and the comparison with a computer-algebra system — with their tests. They are verbatim copies of the authors' repository, differing only in the import lines.

Version 1.2.0 adds five modules that audit a registry of physical-geodesy conventions (permanent tide after Ekman 1989; height systems; the anomaly/disturbance difference; the contraction of the normal-height iteration; the normal height on the model the code actually computes), a gate that ties every formal literal to the Python registry, and the technical note docs/nota_auditoria_formal_convencoes.pdf reporting the outcome: no defect found by proof, two found by reading, one theorem whose bound predicts a measured residual to 0.4 %, and one pin that would have refused a defective coefficient the project once used. The method conclusion is the note's title claim: written against the textbook, the checker proves the textbook; only written against the code does it catch the code.

Version 1.3.0 translates the four Python scripts under python/ and their tests into English (identifiers, docstrings and printed output; the numbers and the logic are unchanged, and the gate that keeps them identical to the authors' repository still holds), and removes an accidental duplication of the README.

This material accompanies a methodological manuscript on distinguishing algebraic identities from independent verification in physical geodesy.
notes: The proofs are elementary: they close with algebraic and elementary-analysis tactics. The contribution is methodological, not mathematical.
